Three parts

What we will answer

1Where does the outside operator walk, and in what order?→ 2What does he read in the field, and when can he trust it?→ 3Why does each hand valve have a normal position, and how is every item named?→

Outside (field) operator = the operator on the plant floor; the panel operator sits at the DCS. NO / NC = normally open / closed · LO / LC = locked (car-sealed) open / closed. P1, P2 = platforms. Tag letters follow ISA-5.1 (part 3).

Interactive · the plant drawn from layout.json (teaching layout, assumed)

Walk round the bay

One structure carries the column and two platforms; everything else stands on the ground, reached from aisles.

Interactive · the route of the round, pick a station

Ten stations, each with a purpose

Each station answers one question about one system: is it lined up, is it running, does the field agree with the DCS?

The order of the round

Follow the heat, then the products, then the utilities

  1. Pot and heatstations 1–3: where the batch boils
  2. Column, up and downstations 4–6: one climb by the ladders
  3. Productsstation 7: where the cut goes
  4. Utilitiesstations 8–10: vacuum, N₂, water

Interactive · route length from the tab's waypoints

How long does one round take?

Ladder climbing taken at a quarter of the walking speed (assumed).

Walking is a few minutes; the time goes into looking and reading, so a careful round takes about half an hour.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The outside operator sees what transmitters cannot.
  • The 3-D plant is built from the layout data.
  • Ten stations follow heat, products, then utilities.
  • Most of a round is spent reading, not walking.

Part 2 · Reading the plant

What does he read in the field, and when can he trust it?

Part 2 · the plan

A number is only as good as its reading

  1. Three kinds of field readinggauge, indicator, second sensor
  2. Reading a dialdivisions and range
  3. Absolute and gauge pressurea vacuum unit reads both
  4. Field against DCS, the rounds sheetcompare, record, report

Where a field number comes from

Not every local reading is independent

ReadingNeeds power?Same as DCS?
Local gauge (PG, TG)nono: independent
Transmitter local displayyesyes: same signal
Second sensor (tag …B)yesno: own element

The seven local gauges are added by the layout; they are not on the P&ID.

Interactive · the seven local gauges, practice needle

Read to one small division

A practice value, not a plant reading: read the plant in Visual plant 3D.

A reading is worth half a small division; a well-chosen gauge reads its normal value in the middle third of the dial.

Interactive · one pressure, two scales

Vacuum in mbar a, discharge in barg

$P_g=P_{abs}-P_{atm},\quad P_{atm}=1013\ \text{mbar}$
$P_{abs}$
from perfect vacuum
mbar a
$P_g$
above atmosphere
barg
$P_{atm}$
atmosphere (standard)
mbar

Below atmosphere a barg gauge goes negative and coarse; vacuum is read in mbar absolute, pump discharges in barg.

Compare, do not correct

Two readings that agree build trust

The rounds sheet turns the walk into a record.

  • Read the field value before looking at the DCS.
  • Agree within a division: record it.
  • Disagree: record both, tell the panel.
  • Never adjust a reading to match.

The rounds sheet of the tab

Checked against the plant at that moment

Rule of the sheetWhy
Checked at the moment of Checka batch keeps moving
Tolerance: a small division or 2 %honest reading error

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Local gauges are independent of the DCS.
  • Read to half a small division.
  • Vacuum is read absolute; discharge pressure as gauge.
  • Record disagreements; never make readings agree.

Hand valves of the layout

Every hand valve has a normal position

Readings settled; now the valves the operator lines up.

Normal positions come from P&ID notes and SOPs; locks are proposed by the layout.

Interactive · pick a valve service

The service decides the normal position

Flow paths stay open, anything that opens the unit to air or bypasses a control stays closed, the critical ones locked.

Interactive · a valve class and an action

May the outside operator move it?

A lock means a permit and the seal register before anyone moves it; the tab refuses an LO valve outright.

Interactive · ISA-5.1 letters on the field items

A tag says what it measures and does

First letter = what is measured, next letters = what the device does; the number ties it to its loop.

The identification exercise

Name the item without its plate

  1. Choose Identifytag plates disappear, blank boxes appear
  2. Pick the tagfrom shape, service, connections
  3. Check stationmarks each box
  4. Gradetarget 90 % over the stations tried

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Every hand valve has a normal position.
  • Service decides it; locks guard the critical ones.
  • Locked valves move only with a permit.
  • Tag letters say what an item measures and does.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the same route every shift: heat, column, products, utilities.

2

Read local gauges first; they do not depend on the DCS.

3

Compare field and DCS; report differences, never hide them.

4

Know each valve's normal position and who may change it.
